note: ape_test is a test-only submodule of ape. It ships only routing + one controller (ApeTestController), with no config, permissions, services, schema or hooks. Its five public routes (all _access TRUE): ape.redirect.301 (/ape_redirect_301, 301 -> /ape_redirect_landing), ape.redirect.302 (/ape_redirect_302, 302 -> landing), ape.redirect.landing (/ape_redirect_landing, renders 'Arrived at your final destination.'), ape.alternative (/ape_alternative) and ape.exclude (/ape_exclude) — stable paths to list in APE's alternatives/exclusions and assert the Cache-Control header. It ships disabled. Because it has no config surface, medium/hard cases are grounded in its live state: introspection reads its enablement and its registered routes/paths; execution enables and uninstalls it, verified against core.extension. Note: on this shared site module enable/uninstall can hang on terminate due to an unrelated broken module, but the operation still persists.

evals.prompt: What does the ape_test submodule provide, and name at least two of the URL paths (endpoints) it registers.
evals.expected_output: It provides test-only endpoints (a controller + routes) to exercise APE's Cache-Control behaviour: /ape_redirect_301, /ape_redirect_302, /ape_redirect_landing, /ape_alternative and /ape_exclude.

evals.prompt: In the ape_test module, what does requesting /ape_redirect_301 do, and where does it send the user?
evals.expected_output: /ape_redirect_301 (ApeTestController::redirect301) issues a 301 redirect to /ape_redirect_landing, which renders 'Arrived at your final destination.' This lets a test assert the Cache-Control header APE applies to 301s.

evals.prompt: Why would I enable ape_test, and should it be enabled on a production site?
evals.expected_output: It exists only to test/verify APE's Cache-Control behaviour (redirects, alternative pages, excluded pages) with stable endpoints; enable it in test/dev, not production.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, is the ape_test module enabled? If so, what URL path does its ape.redirect.301 route serve? Inspect the running site to answer.
evals.expected_output: ape_test is enabled and its ape.redirect.301 route serves the path /ape_redirect_301.

evals.prompt: The ape_test module is enabled on this site. Inspect the running site's routing and list the test paths it registers (besides /ape_redirect_301).
On this Drupal site, enable the ape_test module (the APE testing submodule with the redirect/landing endpoints). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: ape_test is enabled (appears in core.extension; e.g. drush en ape_test -y), so its /ape_redirect_* endpoints resolve.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the ape_test module is currently enabled. Uninstall it (leave the parent ape module untouched). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: ape_test is no longer enabled (absent from core.extension; e.g. drush pmu ape_test -y), while ape remains enabled.
